issues.description: README.rst example changes signature of StorageError.handle in a breaking way
issues.detail: The README diff changes `handle(ex, req, resp, params)` to `handle(req, resp, ex, params)`. Falcon's `add_error_handler` historically expects `(req, resp, ex, params)` in newer versions, but this is unrelated to the PR's stated purpose (adding POST tests). Bundling unrelated README rewrites with a test PR increases regression risk and review burden.

issues.description: FAQ example uses req.stream.read with potentially untrusted Content-Length
issues.detail: The FAQ snippet calls `req.stream.read(req.content_length or 0)` to teach header overriding. This pattern is the very footgun the example example switched away from (to bounded_stream). Teaching `req.stream.read(content_length)` in docs contradicts the simultaneous change in things_advanced.py and may mislead readers.

issues.description: New test relies on AuthMiddleware accepting any token; brittle to example changes
issues.detail: `test_things_advanced` posts with `Authorization: custom-token` and asserts 201/400. This depends on `_token_is_valid` always returning True in the example. If the example is ever tightened (a common follow-up), these tests silently break. Consider asserting against a stable fixture or documenting the dependency.

issues.description: FAQ code block has minor style issues (trailing comma in list, redundant parens in assert)
issues.detail: `headers = [('Content-Length', '1'),]` has a stray trailing comma, and `assert(result.status == ...)` uses function-call style for assert. These are minor but the FAQ is user-facing documentation and should model idiomatic Python.

issues.description: Missing towncrier news fragment despite checklist claim
issues.detail: The PR checklist claims a towncrier fragment was added under `docs/_newsfragments/`, but the diff shows no such file. Either the fragment is missing or it wasn't included in the diff shown; reviewers should verify before merge to keep changelog automation honest.

issues.description: Test does not cover ASGI path despite checklist claiming WSGI+ASGI coverage
issues.detail: The new POST assertions use `testing.simulate_post(advanced.app, ...)` against the single example app. The checklist asserts both WSGI and ASGI paths were updated, but `things_advanced.py` is WSGI-only and no parallel ASGI test was added. Acceptable but worth noting given the explicit checklist claim.

review.summary: The functional change (switching to `req.bounded_stream.read()` in things_advanced.py and adding two POST tests) is small and reasonable. However the PR bundles a large unrelated README.rst restyle that includes a signature change for `StorageError.handle`, which expands scope and risk. The FAQ example also teaches `req.stream.read(content_length)`, which contradicts the bounded_stream change made in the same PR. Minor style nits in the FAQ snippet and a missing/unverified towncrier fragment round out the concerns.
